newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France cargo hit by work to rule.
newsitem.headline: Air France cargo hit by work to rule.

text.p: Air France Cargo said it had placed an embargo on perishables shipments, live animals and urgent freight as a result of a "work to rule" by airline staff at its Charles de Gaulle hub.

"Until further notice, we are not accepting any reservations for any category of freight to be carried on passenger services but will continue to accept non-urgent freight for all-cargo flights," an cargo division official said.
Approximately 70 percent of Air France cargo is carried in the bellyhold of passenger aircraft, industry sources said.

"Work to rule" action by Air France cargo personnel, which began yesterday, was sparked by reports yesterday that the airline was considering transforming its freight division into a subsidiary company.
A meeting of the airline's works council was also addressed yesterday by senior cargo executives in an effort to allay staff fears relating to job losses, a company official said.
"We have made no decision whatsoever on this matter and are not even at the stage of commissioning a study," she added.
The whole idea of subsidiary status, if retained, would be to develop Air France' cargo activities while safeguarding jobs, the official added.

In addition to industrial action by Air France cargo personnel, the airline's flight programme will be disrupted tomorrow as a result of strike action by air traffic controllers. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
